messages.author: 4b63675507b4aa11
messages.subject: Instrumental variable estimation
parts:
Dear All,

I am trying to figure out how to estimate an instrumental variable model using Stan. The attached file is a very simple simulated example in which three variables are involved: y is dependent variable, x is the treatment variable, and z is the treatment assignment (i.e., instrument) variable. The stan code was borrowed from example 23.4 of the ARM code repo (https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/blob/feature/ARM/src/models/ARM/Ch.23/sesame_street1.stan) but is much simpler because I am not doing any multilevel stuff. The model seems to work but I got a lot of warnings saying that:

"Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected becuase of the following issue:
Invalid value of Sigma_yt: Error in function validate transformed params N4stan5agrad3varE: Sigma_ytSigma_yt is not positive definite. Sigma_yt(0,0) is 1.3618914389258178e-17:0.
If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,
but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified."

Should I be worried? Are there ways to improve the code?

Thanks and happy new years!

Best,
Shige

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Instrumental variable estimation
parts:
On 12/27/13, 3:31 PM, Shige Song wrote:
> Dear All,
>
> I am trying to figure out how to estimate an instrumental variable model using Stan. The attached file is a very simple
> simulated example in which three variables are involved: y is dependent variable, x is the treatment variable, and z is
> the treatment assignment (i.e., instrument) variable. The stan code was borrowed from example 23.4 of the ARM code repo
> (https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/blob/feature/ARM/src/models/ARM/Ch.23/sesame_street1.stan) but is much simpler because
> I am not doing any multilevel stuff. The model seems to work but I got a lot of warnings saying that:
>
> "Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected becuase of the following issue:
> Invalid value of Sigma_yt: Error in function validate transformed params N4stan5agrad3varE: Sigma_ytSigma_yt is not
> positive definite. Sigma_yt(0,0) is 1.3618914389258178e-17:0.
> If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the
> sampler is fine,
> but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified."
>
> Should I be worried? Are there ways to improve the code?

No, you shouldn't be worried. We don't know how to convince users
that the message means what it says!

Part of the issue is on our end --- we need to relax the
tolerance on our tests for positive definiteness.

What you do want to check is that your estimates are not
jammed up against parameer boundaries. That is, if you
get rho_yt near -1 or 1, or sigma_t or sigma_y near 0 or 100,
that probably indicates a mismatch of your model to your data.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Instrumental variable estimation
parts:
I'm aware this is a very old thread, but the line

y <- 3 + 1.5*2*z + rnorm(n)

in the script attached should be 

y <- 3 + 1.5*2*x + rnorm(n)

Just in case anyone wants to use this in the future. 

Jim
